transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve felt low and weighed down almost all the time for the last couple of years, and it just never really lifts. It’s like this heavy, flat feeling is constantly with me and I just can't seem to shake it.

During these last couple of years, have there been stretches of at least 2 months when your mood felt mostly back to normal, or has the low mood been there nearly every day without a real break? Have there also been any distinct periods lasting at least 2 weeks when it became much worse than your usual baseline?

No, there haven't been any breaks at all—certainly nothing close to two months of feeling normal. It has just been a steady, continuous heavy feeling since we moved, without any distinct periods where it suddenly got much worse than this baseline.

Along with this long-lasting low mood, have you also had symptoms like low energy, poor self-esteem, trouble concentrating or making decisions, changes in sleep or appetite, or feeling hopeless? Which of these have been present most days?

I struggle constantly with low energy, feeling like I'm wading through molasses even after a full night's sleep. My brain is in a heavy fog, so concentrating on my work or making simple daily decisions feels almost impossible. And honestly, I feel completely hopeless about the future, like this flat, numb feeling is all I'll ever know.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more when you felt unusually energized or upbeat, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt unusually confident or impulsive? Even if it didn’t feel like a problem, has anything like that ever happened?
No, I've never had a period like that at all. My mood has been consistently low and flat, and I've never experienced feeling unusually energized, upbeat, or needing less sleep.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronically depressed mood present nearly every day for the last couple of years, with no symptom-free interval approaching 2 months, and endorses associated symptoms of low energy, poor concentration/indecisiveness, and hopelessness. There is no history of distinct major depressive episodes superimposed on the baseline and no evidence of hypomanic or manic episodes, supporting persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
